{{Short description|Technique in information theory}}

The '''method of types''' is a tool in [[Information Theory | information theory]] and [[Large deviations theory|large deviation theory]] to analyze events from the perspective of the [[empirical measure|empirical distribution]].<ref name="CoverThomas">{{cite book 
|title=Elements of Information Theory 
|publisher=Wiley-Interscience 
|isbn=9780471241959 
|pages=347-355 
|ref=CoverThomas}}</ref><ref name="CsiszarMoT">{{cite journal 
|last1=Csiszár 
|first1=Imre 
|title=The Method of Types 
|journal=IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 
|date=October 1998 
|volume=44 
|doi=10.1109/18.720546 
|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/720546|url-access=subscription 
}}</ref> It classifies events as [[Typical set|typical]] when the empirical distribution closely matches the true distribution. 

It has been used to prove results in [[Error exponents in hypothesis testing|hypothesis testing]], [[Error correction code|channel coding]],<ref name="CsiszarMoT" /><ref name="StanfordLectureNotes">{{cite web |last1=Weissman |first1=Tsachy |title=Lecture 13: Method of Types |url=https://web.stanford.edu/class/ee376a/files/2017-18/lecture_13.pdf |website=web.stanford.edu |publisher=Stanford |access-date=3 May 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250325113446/http://web.stanford.edu/class/ee376a/files/2017-18/lecture_13.pdf | archive-date=25 Mar 2025}}</ref> and [[Universal code (data compression)|universal source coding]],<ref name="CoverThomas" /><ref name="Method Of Types Lecture Notes">{{cite web |last1=Debris-Alazard |first1=Thomas |title=Method Of Types And Applications |url=https://tdalazard.io/infoTheory/S5.pdf |website=tdalazard.io |publisher=Inria, École Polytechnique |access-date=3 May 2026 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251213130935/https://tdalazard.io/infoTheory/S5.pdf |archive-date=13 Dec 2025}}</ref> and it is used to prove [[Sanov's theorem]] in the finite support setting.<ref>{{cite book 
|last1=Dembo 
|first1=Amir 
|last2=Zeitouni 
|first2=Ofer 
|title=Large Deviations Techniques and Applications |date=2010 
|publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg 
|location=Berlin, Heidelberg 
|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-642-03311-7
|isbn=978-3-642-03310-0 
|access-date=11 August 2026}}</ref><ref name="JeffSteifLectureNotes">{{cite web |last1=Steif |first1=Jeff |title=Notes on Information Theory by Jeff Steif |url=https://www.math.chalmers.se/~steif/info.pdf |website=math.chalmers.se |publisher=Jeff Steif |access-date=3 May 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260503142029/https://www.math.chalmers.se/~steif/info.pdf | archive-date=3 May 2026}}</ref> It is often used to simplify complex probability expressions into more natural expressions involving the [[Kullback–Leibler divergence]]. It was popularized by [[Imre Csiszár]],<ref name="CsiszarBio">{{cite web |title=Imre Csiszár |url=https://ethw.org/Imre_Csiszar |website=ethw.org |publisher=Engineering and Technology History Wiki |access-date=20 April 2026 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200104050621/https://ethw.org/Imre_Csiszar | archive-date=4 Jan 2020}}</ref> with the first formal treatment given in the book ''Information Theory: Coding Theorems for Discrete Memoryless Systems''.<ref name="PolyanskiyBook" /><ref name="DiscreteMemorylessChannels">{{cite book |last1=Csiszár |first1=Imre |last2=Körner |first2=János |title=Information Theory: Coding Theorems for Discrete Memoryless Systems |date=1981 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=9780511921889 |edition=2nd}}</ref>. Csiszár claimed that the technique was originally motivated by the large deviation bound described in Hoeffding's seminal paper on multinomial hypothesis testing.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hoeffding |first1=Wassily |title=Asymptotically Optimal Tests for Multinomial Distributions |journal=The Annals of Mathematical Statistics |date=April 1965 |volume=36 |issue=2 |pages=369–401 |doi=10.1214/aoms/1177700150 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-mathematical-statistics/volume-36/issue-2/Asymptotically-Optimal-Tests-for-Multinomial-Distributions/10.1214/aoms/1177700150.full |access-date=11 August 2026|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="CsiszarMoT"></ref>

== Motivating example ==
Given <math>n</math> samples from <math>P</math>, a Bernoulli distribution with probability of success <math>p</math>, there are <math>2^n</math> possible outcomes. We can group outcomes by the number of successful events, since every collection of <math>r</math> successes has the same probability, <math>p^r(1-p)^{n-r}</math>, and there are <math>\binom{n}{r}</math> such events. This can be summarized by considering the empirical distribution <math>P_r = \left(1 - \frac{r}{n}, \frac{r}{n}\right)</math> and the type class <math>T(P_r) = \left\{X^n: \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf{1}\{X_i = 1\} = r\right\}</math>. With some analysis, one finds that 
<math display=block>
\begin{align}
  \mathbb{P}\left[X^n\right] = p^r (1-p)^{n-r} \approx 2^{-n [H(P_r) + D(P_r\|P)]},\\
\mathbb{P}[T(P_r)] = \binom{n}{r} p^r(1-p)^{n-r} \approx 2^{-n D(P_r\|P)},
\end{align}
</math>
where <math>H(P_r), D(P_r\|P)</math> denote the Shannon entropy and relative entropy. These approximations are most accurate when <math>n</math> is taken to be large. A more accruate bound would be 
<math display=block>
(n+1)^{-2} 2^{-n D(P_r\|P)} \leq \mathbb{P}[T(P_r)] \leq 2^{-n D(P_r\|P)}.
</math>

For example, if we wanted to get a rough estimate of the probability of seeing <math>r=400</math> heads in 1000 tosses of a fair coin, we could compute 
<math display=block>
    \begin{align}
    D(P_r\|P) &= 0.6 \log \frac{0.6}{0.5} + 0.4 \log \frac{0.4}{0.5}\\
    &\approx 0.02905
    \end{align}
</math>
which gives us the (loose) approximation
<math display=block>
2^{-1000 * 0.02905} \approx 1.799 * 10^{-9},
</math>
while the true value is 
<math display=block>
\binom{1000}{400}2^{-1000} \approx 4.6339 * 10^{-11}.
</math>
The figure below plots the exact probability and the upper and lower bounds.

[[File:MethodOfTypesBound.svg|thumb|The probability that <math>n</math> i.i.d. samples of a Bernoulli(1/2) random variable will have type (2/5, 3/5), along with the method-of-types bounds [log scale].]]

The method of types generalizes the above example to multivariate distributions.

== Mathematical formulation ==
Let <math>\mathcal{X}</math> be an alphabet with a finite number of elements. We start with a sequence of [[Independent and identically distributed random variables|i.i.d.]] [[Random variable|random variables]] following a finite support distribution <math>Q</math>, <math> X^n = (X_1, \dots, X_n) \sim Q </math>, where <math>X_i\in \mathcal{X}</math>. For this sequence, let <math>N(k|X^n) = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf{1}\{X_i = k\}</math> denote the number of occurrences of the symbol <math>k</math> in the sequence <math>X^n</math>. 

Denote the [[Empirical measure|empirical distribution]] of the samples with <math>P_{X^n}</math>, so that <math>P_{X^n}[k] = \frac{N(k|X^n)}{n}</math>. The sets of sequences having   empirical distribution <math>Q</math>, are called the type classes <math>T(Q) = \{X^n \in \mathcal{X}^n: P_{X^n} = Q\} </math>. To describe the set of all empirical distributions possible from <math>n</math> samples, we use the symbol <math>\mathcal{P}_n</math>, which is a subset of the <math>d-1</math> dimensional [[Simplex|probability simplex]] <math>\mathcal{P}</math>. 

The method of types is built on top of the following results:<ref name="CoverThomas" />
* <math>|\mathcal{P}_n| \leq (n+1)^{|\mathcal{X}|}</math>

* <math> Q[X^n] = 2^{-n \left[H(P_{X^n}) + D(P_{X^n}\|Q)\right]}</math>

* <math> \frac{1}{ (n+1)^{ |\mathcal{X}| } } 2^{n H(Q)} \leq |T(Q)| \leq 2^{n H(Q)}</math>

* <math> \frac{ 1 }{ (n+1)^{|\mathcal{X}| } } 2^{-nD(P\|Q)} \leq Q[T(P)] \leq 2^{-n D(P\|Q)} </math>

Here <math>H(P)</math> denotes the [[Entropy (information theory)|Shannon entropy]], and <math>D(P\|Q)</math> denotes the [[Kullback–Leibler divergence]]. 
The last equation is derived from the previous ones by noticing that every element of <math>T(P)</math> has the same probability when the samples are taken i.i.d. 

These bounds are tight in terms of the error exponent,<ref name="SecondOrderHTesting">{{cite journal 
|last1=Harsha 
|first1=K. V. 
|last2=Ravi 
|first2=Jithin 
|last3=Koch 
|first3=Tobias

|date=October 2025

|issue=10

|doi=10.1109/TIT.2025.3588194 
|url=https://e-archivo.uc3m.es/rest/api/core/bitstreams/5ccc4646-ccb8-428b-8652-cf0347627cf7/content 
|access-date=10 July 2026
|arxiv=2403.03537}}</ref> but may give a loose bound in terms of <math>|\mathcal{X}|</math> and the sub-exponential terms in <math>n</math>.<ref name="BeyondMethodOfTypes">{{cite journal

== Applications ==
The method of types is used for [[hypothesis testing]] problems, when the underlying distributions have finite support<ref name="MethodOfTypesAndHTesting_ClassNote">{{cite web 
|last1=Singh 
|first1=Aarti 
|title=Lecture 21: Hypothesis Testing, Method of Types and Large Deviation 
|url=https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~aarti/Class/10704/lec21-types_largdev.pdf 
|website=www.cs.cmu.edu 
|publisher=Aarti Singh 
|access-date=10 July 2026
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250811041945/http://www.cs.cmu.edu/~aarti/Class/10704/lec21-types_largdev.pdf
|archive-date=11 Aug 2025
}}</ref><ref name="CsiszarMoT"/><ref name="UHT_MiniMaxApproach">{{cite journal |
last1=Feder 
|first1=M. 
|last2=Merhav 
|first2=N. 
|title=Universal composite hypothesis testing: a competitive minimax approach 
|journal=IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 
|date=June 2002 
|volume=48 
|issue=6 
|pages=1504–1517 |doi=10.1109/tit.2002.1003837 
|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/1003837
|access-date=10 July 2026 
|issn=0018-9448
| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260117055521/https://www.eng.tau.ac.il/~meir/articles/43%20Universal%20composite%20hypothesis%20testing%20a%20competitive%20minimax.pdf
|archive-date=17 Jan 2026|url-access=subscription 
}}</ref>, because it provides a tight bound on the error exponent. It was also used to prove some initial conditional limit theorems<ref name="ConditionalLimitTheorems">{{cite journal 
|last1=Csiszar 
|first1=I. 
|last2=Cover 
|first2=T. 
|title=Conditional limit theorems under Markov conditioning 
|journal=IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 
|date=November 1987 |volume=33 |issue=6 |pages=788–801 
|doi=10.1109/TIT.1987.1057385 
|url=https://www-isl.stanford.edu/~cover/papers/transIT/0788csis.pdf 
|access-date=11 August 2026}}</ref>, which are special cases of the general class of limit theorems. The bound on the size of a type class can be used to prove tight bounds on the exact value on [[Binomial coefficient#Bounds and asymptotic formulas|binomial coefficients]]<ref name="CoverThomas"></ref>. It is also used to prove the [[Principle of maximum entropy|principle of maximum entropy]].<ref name="DiscreteProbModels">{{cite book 
|last1=Brémaud 
|first1=Pierre 
|title=Discrete Probability Models and Methods: Probability on Graphs and Trees, Markov Chains and Random Fields, Entropy and Coding 
|page=351
|date=2017 
|publisher=Springer International Publishing 
|location=Cham 
|isbn=978-3-319-43475-9 
|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-319-43476-6 
|access-date=11 August 2026 
|language=en}}</ref>
